title: Fired Rockstar Workers Tell Fans Not to Boycott GTA 6
description: The first Rockstar workers embroiled in a legal battle with the company have urged fans not to boycott GTA 6 to protest on their behalf, pointing to better ways to support them.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## The Anticipation and Controversy Surrounding GTA 6

As one of the most anticipated video game releases in history, Rockstar Games' *GTA 6* consistently commands the attention of the global gaming community. However, beyond the excitement for trailers, gameplay features, and release windows, the internal labor relations and employment practices at Rockstar have also drawn significant scrutiny from media and fans alike.

Recently, a new development has shed light on the complex relationship between disgruntled fans, the studio, and the very workers who have been affected by internal company disputes.

## A Direct Plea from Displaced Workers

According to a report published by IGN Games on August 18, 2026, the first group of Rockstar workers who are currently embroiled in a legal battle with the company have reached out to the fan community with a clear message: do not boycott *GTA 6* in protest on their behalf.

While a segment of the player base has considered boycotting the upcoming blockbuster to show solidarity with affected employees, the workers involved in the legal proceedings have pushed back against this strategy. They emphasize that while solidarity is appreciated, boycotting the game is not the right path forward.

Instead, these workers have indicated that "there’s a better way to support us and hold Rockstar to account." Although the source material does not elaborate on the specific alternative actions, the statement highlights a nuanced perspective from those directly impacted by corporate decisions.

## Navigating Labor Rights and Gaming Culture

This situation underscores the delicate balance within the modern gaming industry. Gamers often look for ways to express their dissatisfaction with corporate practices—such as layoffs or labor disputes—by hitting publishers where it hurts: their sales. Yet, the developers and former employees who actually built the games often harbor a different perspective, hoping that their hard work is still appreciated while they pursue justice through proper legal channels.

As the conversation around studio culture and worker treatment continues to evolve, listening to the desires of the affected workers themselves remains a crucial step for a supportive community.

## Editor's Take

It is commendable that Rockstar workers currently locked in legal battles are urging fans to avoid a blanket boycott of *GTA 6*. This pragmatic approach shows that defending labor rights doesn't have to mean destroying the fruits of collective creative labor. Supporting developers effectively requires thoughtful action, not just reactionary backlash.
